description.narrative: (Uganda): .The Integrated Community Agriculture and.Nutrition (ICAN) activity works with community groups to maximize economic.opportunities for vulnerable households, stabilize access to and.consumption of nutritious diets, and increase social capital by reinforcing.relationships among formal governance systems and communities. Through.collaboration with the private sector and district and local governments, and.increasing the organizational capacity of partnering organizations, ICAN is.laying the foundation for increased self-reliance in Uganda...With FY 2021.funds, ICAN will scale-up its work with community groups to promote resilience..ICAN's mother care groups and adolescent girls' camps will be scaled-up, and.participants will continue to receive family planning and nutrition.interventions. The mother care groups will be linked to Business Service.Providers for training in various enterprises e.g., tailoring, hairdressing and.agricultural enterprises. Diversification of income sources will help the.groups withstand climate-related and other shocks and stresses and increase.their resilience. All ICAN groups will be encouraged to plant multipurpose.trees to curb climate variability, and to use energy saving stoves to minimize.deforestation and associated climate impacts. In hilly areas in the South West,.households will be taught and encouraged to practice terracing and other.climate-smart farming techniques. ICAN will continue to collaborate with health.activities to advance a social and behavioral change curriculum...ICAN will.increase community mobilization by facilitating community members' civil.society engagement to improve their access to health and social protection.services. ICAN will enhance economic opportunities for 116,000 poor households.by improving livelihoods and strengthening connections to markets and financial.services. Participating communities will have stronger networks and services.and be better positioned to respond to shocks..
